title: He Tricked a Real Printer Into Making 100 Million in Real Money — How?
description:
In December 1925, a Lisbon bank clerk noticed something impossible: two 500-escudo notes with the exact same serial number, paper, and ink. Neither was counterfeit. Both were genuine currency, printed months earlier by Waterlow & Sons — the same trusted firm that printed Portugal's official banknotes.

The man behind it was Alves dos Reis, a 27-year-old con artist who forged contracts bearing the Bank of Portugal's seal and convinced Waterlow he had secret authorization for a loan to Portuguese Angola. Believing him, the printer produced 200,000 real banknotes worth 100 million escudos using the actual official plates. Reis laundered the money through a shell bank, buying property, shares, and even a stake in the real Bank of Portugal itself.

The scheme collapsed the Portuguese escudo, destroyed public trust in the currency, and helped trigger the 1926 coup that ended Portugal's democracy for 48 years. Reis served only five years — and to this day, no one knows exactly how much of his fake-real money is still out there.
